string.text: Army tactical rig
Tactical rig
A load-bearing vest designed for carrying "essential" ammunition and personal emergency medical supplies.
A pouch for carrying various items on the belt.
Electronic notebook
An old smartphone converted into an electronic notebook by the repairman Vergas.
Sleeping bag
A lightweight sleeping bag. Waterproof. The model combines the comfort of a blanket-style bag with the high thermal insulation of a mummy bag.
Artist's sketchbook
The sketchbook of a fallen artist, containing drawings and travel notes.
Army flask
A flask with a screw cap on a chain. Made of food-grade aluminum. Comes with a cover. Designed for conveniently carrying liquid.
Decoder
A homemade device for breaking into the electronic door-coding system and capturing the matrix of the code's character set.
Glass in a podstakannik holder
A drinking glass found in the Sanatorium. Clearly from the old days.
Mug
A mug found in the Sanatorium.
Cup
A cup found in the Sanatorium.
Grail
A goblet found in the Sanatorium. Looks like more than one brew was steeped in this one...
Kettlebell with a mug
A kettlebell found in the Sanatorium. A full pood in weight. And how did a mug get fused into it? The Zone, damn it!
Beer mug
A beer mug found in the Sanatorium. Clearly been through an anomaly.
Skis
Old wooden skis with soft bindings for felt boots, and bamboo poles. They don't glide.
Oh right, I found some kind of mug. Crawled all over the whole Sanatorium...
Well, well... Nice! Come on, show me.
Here, take a look. The Sanatorium must've been shaken pretty hard for this to get fused into a kettlebell like that...
Here. A beer mug. Definitely been through an anomaly. You can barely even see it...
It's not a cup, it's a glass. But it does come with a podstakannik holder.
Here, a mug like any other. Clearly someone drank tea from it.
Here it is, the little cup. Careful — it's porcelain. Fine work.
Not exactly a cup, but they clearly had their tea with this.
Oh! That's mine! Hand it over, we'll saw it out of the kettlebell.\nAnd special thanks for not selling it to anyone.
My favorite! Holds as much as a samovar.\nAnd special thanks for not selling it to anyone.
My glass! As I recall, I once swiped it on a train... By accident.\nAnd special thanks for not selling it to anyone.
That's the one, the dear thing. Well, Marked One, you've done me a kindness.\nAnd special thanks for not selling it to anyone.
A collector's piece. This is the very one I had my tea with at the Sanatorium.\nAnd special thanks for not selling it to anyone.
There it is, my imperial goblet!\nAnd special thanks for not selling it to anyone.
Well, take it and enjoy!

Wasn't it a bother, Marked One, lugging such a heavy thing around. The mug's not mine, and I've never met that kettlebell... Although, you know, you've touched me, Marked One. You didn't spare the time or effort crawling through some ruins, all just to do a kindness for an old man who's practically a stranger. Hand the thing over — I'll keep it as a memento of your good deed.

Thanks for the trouble, Marked One, but no offense. This isn't my thing... Although, you know, you've touched me, Marked One. You didn't spare the time or effort crawling through some ruins, all just to do a kindness for an old man who's practically a stranger. Hand the thing over — I'll keep it as a memento of your good deed.

A wonderful little thing, but not mine. Use it yourself... Although, you know, you've touched me, Marked One. You didn't spare the time or effort crawling through some ruins, all just to do a kindness for an old man who's practically a stranger. Hand the thing over — I'll keep it as a memento of your good deed.

Sorry, but that's not the right find. Maybe you'll have better luck next time... Although, you know, you've touched me, Marked One. You didn't spare the time or effort crawling through some ruins, all just to do a kindness for an old man who's practically a stranger. Hand the thing over — I'll keep it as a memento of your good deed.

Don't recognize it. Someone else's thing... Although, you know, you've touched me, Marked One. You didn't spare the time or effort crawling through some ruins, all just to do a kindness for an old man who's practically a stranger. Hand the thing over — I'll keep it as a memento of your good deed.

Some kind of grail. Did you find it in a church? Head still aching? Well, it's obviously not mine... Although, you know, you've touched me, Marked One. You didn't spare the time or effort crawling through some ruins, all just to do a kindness for an old man who's practically a stranger. Hand the thing over — I'll keep it as a memento of your good deed.

Thank you, Marked One. At least there'll be some memento now. Whether of my past life or of your good deed — what matters is that it warms the heart. \nAnd this is for you. I was saving it for my old age, so to speak, but for you — I don't mind parting with it.
Huh... And what would I want skis for? It's May out.
Nah, I've got no use for a gun like that. Keep it.
Don't need the sleeping bag — extra weight.
Thanks, already got one. I don't need a second pair of binoculars.
A battery's a good thing, but right now I've got nowhere to even put it. Sorry.
I'll manage without that belt.
I'd take the container, but it's too heavy. Keep it.
I don't use these rounds. No thanks.
Keep the repair kits. You need them yourself.
These medkits are a bit weak. Maybe toss in some army or scientific ones?
No use for matches right now. A lighter, though, wouldn't hurt.
Good body armor, but mine's better. I'll pass.
I don't want this. Field rations give me heartburn.
Vodka's a good thing, but not now.
These grenades are a bit weak. Got any anti-tank ones?
I don't need anti-rad meds. I'd rather treat myself with vodka.
I don't want these "cat's eyes." They say your kidneys fall out from them.
How do people even drink this? You can't get it down. Vodka's better.
Canned food again... No, spare me.
Hunter's? No need.
The best sausage is a stocking full of cash. Won't trade it for that?
Now that's a waste. A good gun.
A sleeping bag's worth having. You'll regret it, and it'll be too late.
Oh you — that's German optics there...
A battery... That battery is priceless.
Look, belts like these don't just lie around on the road.
You ought to take it to Stas's storeroom, save it for better times.
You're a strange one, Marked One. You can swap it for any kind back at the Bar.
True enough. You'll come to me for repairs yourself.
Medkits like these are a rarity around here.
Look what you're after. Fuel's in short supply these days.
I wouldn't say so, but you're the boss — your call.
Agreed. This is a far cry from a NATO field ration...
Well, suit yourself. Drink vodka, then — give your liver a surprise.
Maybe I should set you up with a gun instead?
A good option, but anti-rad meds are more reliable. In my opinion.
Shame. That's good chemistry. And everyone's liver is still in one piece for now.
Right on the money. But sometimes a can like that saves your life.
As you say. Canned food may taste like crap, but at least it doesn't spoil.
Here you're wrong. It's tasty, and it won't go off.
You'll earn it yourself. All I can throw in is the stocking.
Thanks. Hope this comes in handy.
You're welcome.
Well, I'm off.
Eh, my dear fellow, only the Zone knows how long you'll be trudging through it. You'll likely be ringing in the New Year in these parts.
Bite your tongue, Vergas. But have it your way — I'll take it.
There we go, all good.
Got it, I'm no fool.

Vergas, I still can't get your story out of my head... you know, about how you lay paralyzed in the Sanatorium here, and then an emission got you back on your feet. You asked me to look for your cup too, remember? It's all so strange. What if there really are sometimes special, "healing" emissions, eh?

Listen to you — "healing." It only affected me that way back then; for the others lying in there, oh, things went badly indeed. And as for why it happened to me like that — who the hell knows. And the cup... you know, I'm starting to think maybe I never had any "special" cup at all, that it was just an ordinary hospital one. Or maybe I made it up entirely, to make living a little less frightening. To have at least some proof of my past life.

Yeah, I understand. I'm ready to dig with my own nose myself, just to learn anything about my own past. By the way, since we're on the subject of your cup. I've been to that Sanatorium more than once, but I never came across any dishware. Just three-liter jars, maybe.

Yeah? Pity. And it was you who dealt with that burer that turned up there, right? The youngsters were chattering about it... You're a good man, Marked One — didn't forget my request, and even did a good deed on top of it, one that's useful for everyone. Eh, here goes nothing! I'd been setting something aside for a rainy day, but you surely need it more. Here, take this gift from me.
Well, old man... I don't even know what to say, I wasn't expecting it. Thank you!
